methodology: Experimental, numerical (ABAQUS) and analytical investigations were conducted to compare GFRP-reinforced concrete columns with steel-RC columns under axial compression. Sixteen square columns of 150×150×850mm dimensions were cast using either GFRP or steel reinforcement, with varying stirrup spacings and bar diameters.
research_objective: To investigate the behavior of composite columns reinforced with GFRP bars compared to steel-RC columns under axial compression, comparing load capacity, ductility, and structural behavior.

key_findings.finding: GFRP reinforcement contributes to about 10-12% of the ultimate capacity of GFRP-RC columns, compared to steel-reinforced ones with similar main reinforcement ratio.
Reducing stirrup spacing from 75mm to 50mm increases load carrying capacity by approximately 15% and ductility by about 12%
The proposed modification factor derived from IS 456:2000 enhances predictive accuracy in the Indian context for predicting the capacity of GFRP-reinforced columns.
GFRP-reinforced columns exhibit reduced ductility and a more brittle failure compared to steel-reinforced columns, often characterized by sudden concrete failure and localized bar failure.
Hybrid reinforced columns with both steel and GFRP reinforcements generally demonstrate enhanced load-bearing capacity over columns solely reinforced with GFRP.
Investigation of glass FRP-RC columns under axial load with different reinforcement ratios and types, addressing gaps in existing research.
Comparison of structural performance between GFRP-reinforced concrete columns and steel-reinforced columns, proposing a modified design equation aligned with IS456:2000.
Specimens were modeled using ABAQUS 2017 finite element model (FEM) with a concrete damage plasticity (CDP) model.

properties.value: Comparable to steel-reinforced ones with the same main reinforcement ratio.

properties.context: The difference between analytical and experimental values ranged between 12%and15%
